E.P.Ahammed, E.P.Traders, Kalikadavu Pilicode. By Advs.Sri.A.V.James Sri.P.Dalbi Emmanuel Smt.C.C.Jancy Respondent(S)/Complainant: -------------------------- 1. The State Of Kerala, Rep. R1-2 By Public Prosecutor Sri.V.S.Sreejith Abdul Razak vs The State Of Kerala on 18 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166567721/ 1 This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 18-01-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: Scl. texts.facts: The accused in C.C.No.313 of 2004 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class-I, Hosdurg, has filed this revision petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Section 16 (1-A) (i) r/w Sections 7(i) and 2(ia) (j) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 21.3.2000, PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 600 gram of Ragi from the shop of the first accused. The second accused was the person who supplied the said food item to the first accused. After sampling as per rules, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis. The Public Analyst after analysis filed Ext.P12 report stating that the sample contained a synthetic colour sunset yellow under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and therefore the sample was adulterated. Thereafter, on the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis. Ext.P16 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would also show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for the food item and was therefore adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW6 were examined and Exts.P1 to P23 were marked for the prosecution. Exts.C1 to C3 were also marked as court exhibits. Ext.D1 was marked on the side of the defence.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext.P16 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.
